title: What It Was All For
intro: Right. You have been playing whole games without anybody telling you how they are decided, which is not fair on you.
When neither of you can find a move worth playing, you both pass, and then you count. Surrounded empty points, plus stones you took off. Highest total wins.

steps.instruction: That wall is one stone short of sealing the corner. Finish it.
steps.hint: The top of the wall, against the edge.
steps.explanation: Nine points, and they are yours because nothing of White's can live in there. That is territory -- not stones you own, but empty space nobody else can use.

steps.instruction: Two white stones have got inside. They are on one liberty. Take them.
steps.explanation: Two prisoners, and they are worth a point each at the end -- on top of the points they were sitting on, which are now empty and yours. A stone you capture is worth double: it stops being their territory and starts being yours.

steps.instruction: A bigger corner, and the same missing stone. Close it.
steps.explanation: Twelve points for eight stones, where the last one was nine points for seven. One stone further out and the corner got half again as big. That arithmetic is the whole endgame, and it is why I win games I have no business winning.

outro: Territory, plus prisoners, plus komi for White. Count it before you resign and count it before you pass -- most people at your strength resign games they are winning.
Nobody counts at the start. Everybody counts at the end. The good players start counting somewhere in the middle, and that is the only difference.
